headline: The widely promoted Ukrainian Lima electronic warfare (EW) system, which was allegedly capable of disrupting even Kh-47M2 Kinzhal air-launched ballistic missiles, is now under investigation after authorities found that it failed to meet its declared specifications. According to the investigation, Lima failed to demonstrate the claimed effectiveness against Geran loitering munitions. Between September 2023 and June 2024, LLC Okhrannoe Agentstvo KASKAD sold EW systems to Ukraine’s Ministry of Defense and critical infrastructure facilities for more than UAH 820 million, according to a ruling by the Kyiv Court of Appeal. The cost of installing equipment to protect a single facility ranged from UAH 20 million to UAH 100 million. The systems were guaranteed to provide protection against Geran loitering munitions and Kalibr cruise missiles. It was also claimed that Lima had passed tests conducted by the General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, demonstrated its effectiveness, and could be integrated with a centralized control point. However, the investigation found that the reality was very different: Lima had never undergone the claimed tests, had not been used in combat, and the supposed centralized control point did not exist. Further testing confirmed that Lima was incapable of countering the eight-element Controlled Reception Pattern Antenna (CRPA) Kometa used on Geran loitering munitions, let alone the 12- and 16-channel CRPA systems now deployed on Russian drones, guided aerial bombs, cruise missiles, and ballistic missiles. This leaves us with two possible conclusions: either the Kinzhal’s warhead malfunctioned, or the video was AI-generated. After verification, the CCTV footage appears to be authentic, with no signs of AI generation or manipulation, reinforcing the first possibility, that the warhead simply malfunctioned.

headline: Ukraine’s Main Directorate of Intelligence (GUR/HUR) has published what it claims are fragments of the Russian 3M22 Zircon hypersonic missile. According to Ukrainian intelligence, the missile is equipped with a 3B222 active radar seeker manufactured by NPP Radar MMS. According to the GUR, the Zircon uses a combined guidance system. During most of its flight, it relies on an inertial navigation system, while near the target, its onboard radar activates to refine the target’s position. The photos also show what appears to be a flat antenna array made up of numerous small radiating elements. If the image is indeed of the Zircon’s antenna, its compact design is particularly notable given the missile’s high speed. Radar MMS also produces active radar seekers for other Russian weapons. The GUR, for example, links the company to the 9B918 seeker used on the Iskander-M and the U559 seeker used on the Kh-59M2/M2A. The GUR also claims that the 3M22 Zircon is a conventional two-stage ballistic missile rather than a cruise missile. It uses separate solid-fuel boost and sustainer engines, carries a 120 kg warhead, and has a claimed range of up to 1,000 km.

headline: RT by @sentdefender: According to the Wall Street Journal, Army Secretary Dan Driscoll is expected to leave his post by the end of the year, or possibly sooner, after months of reported tension with Secretary of War Pete Hegseth. Driscoll has served about 18 months and developed a close working relationship with former Army Chief of Staff Gen. Randy George. The two pushed the Army toward greater use of commercial technology and lessons from Ukraine, including integrating commercially available systems more rapidly into military operations. George was abruptly fired by Hegseth in April and has not been replaced by a Senate-confirmed successor. Gen. Christopher LaNeve is currently serving as acting Army chief of staff. Driscoll's departure would therefore leave both of the Army's top civilian and uniformed leadership positions without Senate-confirmed permanent leaders. The reported split also appears to reflect a broader disagreement over Army transformation. Driscoll had advocated adopting Ukrainian style approaches to commercial technology and battlefield innovation, while his relationship with Hegseth reportedly deteriorated after Driscoll became involved in efforts to arrange senior level visits and Army reform discussions. There has been no official confirmation of Driscoll's departure. The Pentagon and Driscoll's representatives declined to comment. Source: https://www.wsj.com/politics/national-security/army-secretary-expected-to-step-down-by-years-end-d7477efb

She described the operation as the sixth suspected shadow-fleet vessel boarded by EU forces in recent months. Russia's shadow fleet consists largely of older tankers whose ownership and links to Russia are often obscured through shell companies and other arrangements. The vessels are used to continue Russian oil exports despite Western sanctions. Kallas said the EU intends to continue disrupting the network, calling shadow fleet oil sales an important source of revenue for Russia's war in Ukraine. Source: https://www.newsweek.com/european-forces-seize-sixth-oil-tanker-linked-to-russian-shadow-fleet-12386290

headline: U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) has issued a fact check following Iranian claims that a tanker struck naval mines in the Strait of Hormuz, calling the report false and stating that no ships have struck mines in the Strait. The claim comes amid renewed tensions following the second Kuwaiti tanker to be struck by projectiles while transiting the Strait over the weekend. It also follows the U.S. strike on Larak Island on August 30, where CENTCOM said it destroyed two Iranian rocket launchers after IRGC personnel were observed preparing to launch rockets carrying sea mines into the Strait. Iran subsequently retaliated with ballistic-missile strikes against U.S. forces in Jordan. Jordanian authorities said eight missiles launched from Iran toward Jordanian territory were intercepted, with no casualties or property damage reported.

headline: The Pentagon has placed several conservative military veterans with large social media followings in civilian roles within the department, according to The Washington Post, which reviewed Pentagon records and spoke with people familiar with the assignments. Among those identified are retired Air Force Col. Rob Maness (@RobManess) and retired Army Col. Kurt Schlichter (@KurtSchlichter) , both of whom have active government email accounts and are assigned to the office of Undersecretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness Anthony Tata. Retired Army Col. Thomas Anderson, who writes online as @CynicalPublius, was also previously listed in the office. The Post reports that the individuals have been serving as either special government employees or highly qualified experts. The precise duties, compensation and start dates for the assignments have not been disclosed. The assignments appear to intersect with several Pentagon initiatives focused on military education and personnel policy. Maness, Schlichter and Anderson participated in a Senior Service College Task Force review at the Army War College in May. The task force was established to examine what Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth described as “toxic” or “woke” ideology at senior service colleges. The disclosure is notable because the three have maintained significant public profiles as commentators and, in several cases, have publicly supported Hegseth's policies. The Post also reports that some of their government affiliations were not disclosed in their recent public commentary. Separately, conservative influencer Jennica Pounds, who writes as DataRepublican (@DataRepublican), disclosed that she became a Defense Department special government employee in July after previously holding a journalist credential in Hegseth's Pentagon press corps. The Pentagon has declined to publicly identify the roles or confirm whether the individuals are receiving taxpayer-funded compensation. Thus far, the available reporting establishes their government affiliations but does not establish that they were hired specifically to promote partisan messaging or that their social-media activity is being directed by the Pentagon. Source: https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/08/30/pentagon-secretly-installs-military-influencers-civilian-roles/

headline: Niger's army, backed by Russian paramilitary forces, has regained control of a key military airbase after mutinous soldiers attacked it a day earlier. Three sources told Reuters that Africa Corps played a key role in helping pro-government forces retake the base. Algeria's defence ministry said it sent four fighter jets and other equipment to help Niger's army in "countering the attempt to destabilize the brotherly nation." The unrest began early Saturday, when sustained gunfire and explosions rang out across several areas of the capital, including the airport and near the presidency, in what four sources described as an attack by mutinous soldiers.
